subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
subtype: Friend × Being envied as the one who is struggling [Receiver]
passage:
I'm Rashmi, and I was at the next table in the canteen when Jyoti said to Ankita, "You've got it easy. An offer letter, and you still complain?" Ankita put down her fork. I expected an argument.

Instead Ankita said, "That sounds like a heavy month for you. Tell me." Jyoti talked for a long time about three rejections and an interview where the words simply froze. Ankita listened, then said, "The offer doesn't mean it's been simple. I'm sleeping badly and I'm scared of the job itself." No speech about working harder.

Later Ankita asked, "Want to do a mock interview on Saturday?" Jyoti shrugged, then said okay. I can't tell what Jyoti felt in the moment, but the shoulders came down.

qa.q: What did Ankita offer to do on Saturday?
What might Jyoti have been feeling when saying "You've got it easy", and what is uncertain?
qa.a: Discouraged and possibly envious after three rejections and a frozen interview. Rashmi can only see behaviour, so it cannot be known for sure.

qa.q: What did Ankita do that helped?
qa.a: Ankita listened first, shared an honest difficulty of their own, and offered specific help without pity or a lecture.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Ankita to be told, "You've got it easy"?
qa.a: Probably stinging and misunderstood, yet Ankita chose to hear Jyoti out and admitted to sleeping badly and feeling scared.

grounding: A struggling friend feels Ankita has it easier; Ankita listens, shares honestly about own difficulty and offers help without pity, seen by an observer.

passage:
Sunday night
Gargi snapped at me in the library today. "Easy for you, your dad pays for coaching, you don't have to do tuitions." Then she went quiet and packed up.
It stung, mostly because it's half true. I don't teach three kids every evening like she does. But I also failed Maths II last sem and have a re-exam in six weeks, which I haven't told anyone.
I followed her to the bus stop. No speech. I said, "You're right that I don't have to earn. I also failed Maths II, and I'm scared of the re-exam." She stared at me. "You?"
We sat on the bench through the next three buses. She told me she sleeps five hours a night. I offered my coaching notes, and she said only if she could help me with integration, which she's brilliant at. Deal.
— Sunaina

qa.q: How many kids does Gargi teach every evening?
How did Sunaina feel when Gargi snapped?
qa.a: Stung, because it was half true, and privately scared about the Maths II re-exam.

qa.q: How did Sunaina offer help without pity or a lecture?
qa.a: By first sharing the failed paper honestly, then trading the coaching notes for Gargi's help with integration.

qa.q: How does Gargi see Sunaina's life at first?
qa.a: As easier and more comfortable, with coaching paid for, while Gargi tutors every evening and sleeps five hours.

grounding: Shows a struggling friend feeling you have it easier, and responding by listening, sharing your own difficulty honestly and helping without pity.

Jahnavi: hey. you ok? that smiley feels a bit heavy
Raghav: 40 applications. 2 calls. 0 offers
Raghav: and everyone i know is posting office pics
Jahnavi: that sounds exhausting. i'm sorry
Jahnavi: honestly, the office pics are the best 5 minutes of my week. my manager tore my first report apart and i cried in the washroom
Raghav: wait really
Jahnavi: really. not the same as job hunting, i know. just saying it isn't all pics
Raghav: ok that helps, weirdly
Jahnavi: want to do a mock interview on saturday? no pressure, no pep talk
Raghav: yes. and thanks for not saying "it'll happen, just stay positive"
Jahnavi: 😅 wouldn't dare

qa.q: How many applications has Raghav sent?
What does Raghav's "must be nice" with a smiley suggest about how Raghav feels?
qa.a: Envious and exhausted, hiding frustration behind a smiley.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi do instead of lecturing or showing off?
qa.a: Jahnavi listened, shared a hard moment from work honestly, and offered a no-pressure mock interview.

qa.q: How does Raghav see Jahnavi after the reply?
qa.a: Less as someone who has it easy; hearing about Jahnavi's struggles "helps, weirdly", and Raghav accepts the mock interview.

grounding: Illustrates being envied by a struggling friend and answering with listening, honest sharing and practical help rather than showing off.
